_note: ZERO GRAVITY - the level property `no_gravity`, and the last of the four things that
stopped a converted level starting. It is a MOVEMENT MODE, not a switch, which is why
the port refused these eighteen levels rather than carrying the flag as it carries
`darkest`. One flag turns on three separate things, and a level missing any one of them
looks like a level that works:
1. WORLD GRAVITY BECOMES V2_ZERO, against (0, scale(10)) otherwise. Nothing in the
level falls - not the player, not a crate, not a minion.
2. MainCharacter::update SKIPS ScreenPad::update ENTIRELY. The two walking buttons do
nothing. There is no walking at all in these levels.
3. PortalManager::managePortalInsertion calls applyImpulse, and that is how the player
moves. Every tap the manager ACCEPTS shoves the character away from where it aimed.
Started with only the first, every level would be a room the player floats in with no way
to move and no way to finish. That is what this file's numbers exist to prevent.
The property on the level_properties node, read exactly as `darkest` is. The original
reads the same flag in four places: the world's gravity, MainCharacter,
GameStateController, and PortalManager - which is what makes it a mechanic rather than
a rendering flag.
setGravity(V2_ZERO) when the flag is on. Zero is not a tunable here: the mode IS zero
gravity, and Zerog::LoadRules refuses a file that says otherwise rather than obeying it.
The port sets its registry's PhysicsSettings to this, where a normal level gets
Units::kRemakeWorldGravityPx (980). Both are the WORLD's; the player's own fall came
from Player::Steer, which these levels do not run at all.
PortalManager::applyImpulse, bytes 142841..143178, decoded in full:
SetLinearVelocity(GetLinearVelocity() + normalize(playerPos - finalPos) * scale(1.4))
An ADD onto the existing velocity (GetLinearVelocity at instruction 48, opAdd at 51,
SetLinearVelocity at 57), so shots accumulate and DRIFT IS THE MECHANIC. Without the
add, every tap would reset the player's motion instead of building on it.
WHY 1.4 NEEDS NO CONVERSION. `scale` is SGlobalScale::scale (bytes 5809..5878), which
is one multiply by m_scaleFactor; m_scaleFactor is GetScreenSize().y / m_absoluteSize
(updateScaleFactor, bytes 5592..5699), and m_absoluteSize is 480 (the constructor,
bytes 5032..5158). At the 480-tall reference the call is the number itself. The SAME
wrapper wraps the world's gravity as scale(10), and Units.hpp already has that 10
decoded as Box2D's DEFAULT_GRAVITY in metres per second squared - so the 1.4 is metres
per second too, and the engine's velocities already are. 70 px/s at kPixelsPerMetre 50,
for anyone reading it beside the remake's pixel numbers (its walk is a guessed 160).
A DIVERGENCE, RECORDED RATHER THAN MATCHED. Because m_scaleFactor is screen height over
480, the original's recoil got STRONGER on a taller screen - 1.4 at 480, 3.15 at 1080.
That is a resolution bug, not a mechanic, and the port takes the reference value.
A SECOND, SMALLER DIVERGENCE. The original aims the recoil away from `finalPos`, the
destination computePortalFinalPos worked out; the port aims it away from the tap itself
(Portals::Flight::toPx). They differ only where the destination was clamped.
WHEN IT FIRES. managePortalInsertion instruction 158 loads m_noGravity and 161 jumps
past the call when it is false, so the shove happens ONLY in these levels. The call at
166 sits AFTER the hasFailed join at 157 - the vibrate block at 149-156 is the only
thing on the failed side - so EVERY ACCEPTED TAP SHOVES, whether or not the shot goes
on to open a portal. The port applies it in Portals::State::Shoot, which is the same
seam: the tap, before the shot has resolved.
Measured, not inferred: 18 levels set the flag, level1c through level18c, and they are
exactly the eighteen chapter-4 levels that did not start. The other fourteen are
level0c, level27c, and the twelve `darkest` levels - 18 + 14 = 32, which is the whole
chapter.
THREE OF THE EIGHTEEN also place `gravity_agent` / `gravity_agent.ent`: level16c,
level17c and level18c. That is the `gravity_well` role in entity_roles.json ("local
gravity well of radius `radius`, chapter 4 only"), and the port does not play it, so
those three start and are reported inert rather than playing. The same role is why
level20c and level27c do not play, so gravity_well is one step covering five levels and
it is separate from this one. Its callbacks are all in one file - ETHCallback_
gravity_agent.angelscript, holding ETHCallback_gravity_agent, retrieveRondaboutCount,
computeRoundabout and ETHCallback_gravity_area.
The per-level PLACEMENT counts are deliberately not written here. test_mp_start prints
them, and it counts nodes; counting grep lines instead is the mistake torch.json
records, and it is not being made a third time.
What the eighteen already hold that the port DOES play: shock_field in level3c, 4c, 5c,
6c, 7c, 11c, 13c, 14c and 18c; carranca in level12c and level13c; barrel_bomb.ent in
level9c and level15c; and a fire_diamond.ent in level15c. All built.
